result: The authors generated and validated floxed Lrrk1 and Lrrk2 mice using northern, RT-PCR, and western analyses to confirm deletion of the floxed alleles results in null mutations at both mRNA and protein levels.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledged the rigorous validation of the conditional knockout alleles. Reviewer 1 noted 'The authors provide a rigorous validation' and Reviewer 3 stated 'the new data around the characterization of the germline-deleted LRRK1 and LRRK2 mice add confidence that LRRK1 and LRRK2 can be deleted using the genetic approach.' The editor confirmed the mice are 'validated conditional double KO (cDKO) mice.'

result: Cre-mediated recombination occurs in 99% of TH+ DA neurons in the SNpc and is restricted to DA neurons in Slc6a3-Cre mice.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly stated 'The authors provide a rigorous validation showing that the Driver (DAT-Cre) is expressed in most DAergic neurons in SN.' The GFP reporter data showing 99% colocalization with TH+ neurons was not challenged by any reviewer.

result: DA neuron-restricted Lrrk cDKO mice exhibit normal mortality, body weight, and brain weight at all ages examined (2-24 months).
evaluation: The editor noted this is a key distinction from germline DKO mice, stating 'it is the loss of LRRK1 and LRRK2 expression within the SNpc DA cells that is not well tolerated' while the mice have normal health parameters. Reviewer 1 confirmed 'the mouse genetics and experimental analysis were performed rigorously, and the results were statistically sound and compelling.'

result: DA neuron-restricted Lrrk cDKO mice develop age-dependent loss of DA neurons in the SNpc, with progressive reduction of TH+ and NeuN+ neurons at 20 and 24 months but not at 15 months.
evaluation: All reviewers accepted this core finding. Reviewer 1 stated 'the authors show that the number of DA neurons is average at 15 but significantly decreased at 20 months of age.' Reviewer 2 confirmed 'cDKO mice developed a late reduction of TH+ neurons in SNpc that partially correlated with the reduction of NeuN+ cells.' The editor affirmed the article 'presents solid data demonstrating that it is the loss of LRRK1 and LRRK2 expression within the SNpc DA cells that is not well tolerated.'

result: DA neurodegeneration in Lrrk cDKO mice is accompanied by increased apoptosis in the SNpc, with a ~2-fold increase in active Caspase-3+/TH+ apoptotic DA neurons at 24 months.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly noted 'the authors show that the number of apoptotic neurons is increased by ~2X in aged SN, demonstrating increased ongoing cell death.' The editor mentioned 'the biochemical mechanisms underlying the reason for the apoptotic cells noted in this study' as a topic for future work, implicitly accepting the apoptosis finding.

result: DA neurodegeneration in Lrrk cDKO mice is accompanied by age-dependent decreases in TH+ dopaminergic terminals in the striatum, with reduced TH immunoreactivity at 24 months but not at 15 months.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 initially requested this data ('it might be beneficial to show the status of DAergic markers in the striatum') and in the revision stated 'They now show that TH levels in the striatum decrease with SNpc neurons,' confirming satisfaction with the added data. This addresses the concern about axon and terminal loss preceding cell body loss in degenerative conditions.

result: TH+ neurons in the locus coeruleus (LC) are preserved in Lrrk cDKO mice at 24 months, and there is no Cre-mediated recombination in the LC, supporting the cell-intrinsic nature of DA neuron loss in the SNpc.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 noted 'The degeneration is limited to DA neurons as LC neurons are not lost, and this population does not express DAT.' This finding was not challenged and supports the specificity of the phenotype to SNpc DA neurons where Cre is expressed.

result: DA neurodegeneration in Lrrk cDKO mice is accompanied by elevated microgliosis in the SNpc at 15, 20, and 25 months, suggesting a cell-extrinsic microglial response to pathophysiological changes in DA neurons.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 stated 'the authors show...activated microglia' as part of the phenotype. The finding that microgliosis occurs despite LRRK expression being unaffected in microglia was not challenged and supports the interpretation of a secondary response to DA neuron pathology.

result: Unlike germline DKO mice, Lrrk cDKO mice show similar numbers of electron-dense vacuoles in SNpc neurons compared to controls, suggesting LRRK in non-DA neurons may play a more prominent role in autophagy-lysosomal pathway regulation.
evaluation: The editor explicitly noted 'the LRRK1/LRRK2 KO mice did not replicate the dramatic increase in autophagic vacuole numbers previously noted in the germline global LRRK1/LRRK2 KO mice.' Reviewer 2 similarly stated 'Unlike the constitutive DKO mice described earlier, cDKO mice did not replicate the dramatic increase in autophagic vacuole numbers.' This distinction was accepted by all reviewers.

result: Lrrk cDKO mice at 10 months exhibit deficits in motor coordination in the challenging 10 mm beam walk test (more hindlimb slips and longer traversal time) but perform normally in the less challenging 20 mm beam walk and pole test.
evaluation: While not extensively discussed by reviewers, the behavioral data was not challenged. Reviewer 3 noted 'new data to address concerns regarding...the functional impact of the modest loss of TH+ neurons' and stated 'The new data provides additional support for the author's claims,' implicitly accepting the motor coordination findings.

result: At 22 months, both Lrrk cDKO and control mice perform poorly in the challenging narrow beam walk test with no significant differences between genotypes, suggesting the test is not optimal to reveal subtle differences at this age.
evaluation: This finding was not challenged by reviewers. The interpretation that aged mice of both genotypes perform poorly is a reasonable conclusion from the data presented, though reviewers did not specifically comment on this aspect.

result: These findings provide evidence for the cell-intrinsic requirement of LRRK in DA neurons and demonstrate a cell-autonomous role of LRRK in support of DA neuron survival in the SNpc of the aging brain.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed this central conclusion. Reviewer 1's summary stated 'This is an important work showing that loss of LRRK function causes late-onset dopaminergic neurodegeneration in a cell-autonomous manner.' The editor confirmed 'it is the loss of LRRK1 and LRRK2 expression within the SNpc DA cells that is not well tolerated as it was previously unclear from past work whether neurodegeneration in the LRRK double knock out (DKO) was cell autonomous.'

result: LRRK2 mutations may impair its protection of DA neurons, leading to DA neurodegeneration in PD, though it remains possible that the physiological role of LRRK in DA neuron survival may be irrelevant to how LRRK2 mutations cause PD.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 raised a significant concern: 'The model has no construct validity since loss of function mutations of LRRK2 are well tolerated in humans and do not lead to Parkinson's disease.' This directly challenges the relevance of the loss-of-function findings to PD pathogenesis. The authors acknowledge this uncertainty in their own discussion, and reviewers did not fully endorse the mechanistic link to PD mutations.

result: Western analysis showed significant reduction of LRRK1 and LRRK2 proteins in the ventral midbrain but not in the cerebral cortex of DA neuron-specific Lrrk cDKO mice at 2-3 months.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 noted 'LRRK levels are decreased selectively in the ventral midbrain' as part of the rigorous validation. Reviewer 1 initially raised a concern about LRRK1 expression levels in SNpc DA neurons but in revision stated 'the authors provide a convincing case that LRRK1 function is important in SNpc DA neurons,' accepting the functional relevance despite expression level questions.
